advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tie the docs count assertion to the live registry cardinality (e.g. derive it from CANONICAL_LLM/load_criteria) so an added/removed criterion fails the test.
evidence: docs/plan-review-gate.md:148: 'Each of the 44 criteria (the F/E/G/A judgment criteria, the T1–T15'
tests/unit/test_guides.py:144: assert "Each of the 44 criteria" in gate_doc
ABSENCE: the test never derives 44 from len(CANONICAL_LLM)/registry, so it only confirms the string was typed, not that 44 is correct or will stay correct.
advisory.finding: The '44 criteria' count in docs/plan-review-gate.md is guarded only by a literal string-presence assertion, not by comparison to the live registry cardinality, so a future criterion addition/removal would leave the doc stale without any test failing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the T15 guidance slice to the actual bullet (e.g. up to the next '- **' marker) instead of a fixed 1000-char window.
advisory.finding: The stack-agnostic negative assertions inspect a fixed 1000-char window from the 'T15' index rather than the T15 bullet's own bounds, so they can span adjacent guide bullets and become fragile if unrelated later text introduces 'Terraform'/'Docker' within that window.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the hard-coded prose-literal assertions in `test_hand_authored_gate_doc_names_current_overlay_range_and_count` with a check that derives the criteria count and overlay range from the registry (e.g. compute the count/range from `load_criteria`/the routing index and assert the doc agrees), so it catches real drift rather than pinning author wording.

search_files for '44 criteria' returns only docs/plan-review-gate.md:148 and the test itself — the number is not derived from the actual criteria registry, so a real count mismatch (e.g. true count 43 while prose still says 44) would pass
Rewording the prose to e.g. 'the 44 review criteria (T1 through T15 overlays)' with no observable-behavior change breaks the test — refactoring-violation criterion (a)
advisory.finding: `test_hand_authored_gate_doc_names_current_overlay_range_and_count` asserts the exact narrative wording 'Each of the 44 criteria' and 'T1–T15 triggered overlays' from the hand-authored doc against a hard-coded copy of the same literal. No non-human consumer parses these prose tokens and nothing derives the count/range from the registry, so the test cannot catch a true count or overlay-range regression (it only detects a behavior-preserving reword of the doc) — a change-detector with regression blindness.
scenarios: A future criterion is added/removed but the doc prose is edited to a different phrasing than the literal, or the prose count drifts from the true registry count
A copy-editing pass rewords the sentence without changing meaning
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute the expected criteria count and overlay-range from the criteria registry (the same source the count describes) and assert the doc reflects that derived value, rather than asserting a fixed sentence literal that duplicates the doc text.
